name: status
description: App overview: product/version, scene, screen size, fps, time scale, UI panels, available input methods, active probes, last event seq. Call first.

name: ui_tree
description: Dump the live UI: UI Toolkit panels and uGUI canvases (what is really on screen, incl. elements created from code). One line per element: #id Type "name" .classes "text" =value [x,y,w,h] flags. '*' marks interactive elements. Coordinates are screen pixels (top-left origin).

root.description: Only the subtree of this element id (#12 or 12).

id.description: Only the subtree of the element with this id from ui_tree / ui_find (the number after #). Same as root=#id.

maxNodes.description: Max printed lines (default 300), shared equally between the UI panels and canvases.

compact.description: Hide anonymous wrappers and control internals (default true).

name: ui_find
description: Search elements. All given filters must match.

type.description: Type name, e.g. Button, TextField, ScrollView.

name: ui_inspect
description: Everything about one element: classes, enabled/visible state, value, layout, resolved style, ancestors, and a hit-test telling which element actually receives a click at its center (detects overlap).

id.description: Element id from ui_tree / ui_find (the number after #). Ids >= 1000000 are uGUI objects.

name.description: Element name (exact match preferred, then substring). Alternative to id.

text.description: Visible text of the element (substring). Alternative to id.

x.description: Screen X in pixels, origin top-left (same space as screenshots at scale 1). Alternative to id.

y.description: Screen Y in pixels, origin top-left.

name: ui_click
description: Click an element or a screen point (move, press, release). Returns the UI events that resulted, so you can tell if the click registered.

id.description: Element id from ui_tree / ui_find (the number after #). Ids >= 1000000 are uGUI objects.

name.description: Element name (exact match preferred, then substring). Alternative to id.

text.description: Visible text of the element (substring). Alternative to id.

x.description: Screen X in pixels, origin top-left (same space as screenshots at scale 1). Alternative to id.

y.description: Screen Y in pixels, origin top-left.

holdMs.description: Hold the button this long before release (long press).

modifiers.description: Held modifiers: any of shift, ctrl, alt, cmd.

method.description: 'event' (default): synthesize UI Toolkit events, deterministic, UI only. 'input': inject through the Input System virtual mouse/keyboard (also reaches uGUI and gameplay code).

description: Type text as keystrokes into the given (or currently focused) element. Falls back to setting the value directly if keystrokes had no effect.

name.description: Element name (exact match preferred, then substring). Alternative to id.

x.description: Screen X in pixels, origin top-left (same space as screenshots at scale 1). Alternative to id.

name: key
description: Press, hold or release a key like a real keyboard. Key names are UnityEngine.KeyCode names (Return, Escape, Tab, Space, Backspace, LeftArrow, W, Alpha1, LeftShift, F5...; Enter and Digit1 work too). method=auto (default) picks the route: the focused UI Toolkit element; else the selected uGUI object (Return/Space submit, Escape cancels, arrows and Tab move the selection, a text field takes every key); else gameplay input, read by Input.GetKey or Input System actions.

holdMs.description: For press: how long to hold.

modifiers.description: Held modifiers: any of shift, ctrl, alt, cmd.

method.description: auto (default) | event: UI Toolkit events | input: Input System virtual keyboard (Input System Key names) | os: real key events posted to the game window (macOS and Windows builds), for gameplay code even while a UI object is selected.

name: play
description: Play the game for a stretch in one call: each step holds/taps keys, presses an Input System action, tilts the left stick or moves the mouse for its duration, frame by frame inside the game; use it for walking, jumping and looking around. Example: {"steps":[{"hold":["W","LeftShift"],"ms":800},{"tap":["Space"],"look":[200,0],"ms":300}],"observe":["/Player:Transform.position"]}.

steps.description: Up to 100 steps, at most 60000 ms in total. Step fields (all optional): hold (Input System Key names held during the step: W, LeftShift, Space...), tap (keys pressed for one frame at the start), action (Input System action name or Map/Action; its keyboard or mouse-button binding is held during the step), move ([x,y] left gamepad stick, -1..1), look ([dx,dy] total mouse delta over the step, +y up), ms (duration; default one frame).

observe.description: State paths (as in state_get) read after every step.

stopWhen.description: {"path":"<state path>","equals":"<value>"}: stop as soon as the value matches (checked every frame; without equals, when the path resolves).

timeoutMs.description: Stop the whole call after this many ms, releasing the keys it holds (default: when the steps end).

name: input_actions
description: List the game's Input System controls: action maps, actions, their bindings and current values, from active PlayerInput components and enabled actions; call it before play to learn the action names. Example: {}.

name: screenshot
description: Capture the real framebuffer (exactly what is displayed). With annotate=true, interactive elements are outlined and labelled with their ids. With camera, renders only what that camera sees (no overlay UI).

camera.description: Camera name, GameObject path or #u id (see render_scene).

name: frames_record
description: Ring-buffer recording of frames for frame-by-frame analysis.

fps.description: Capture rate (default 5; use 0 for every frame).

onlyChanges.description: Skip frames identical to the previous one (default true).

name: frames_get
description: Fetch recorded frames as images (max 8 per call). Use frames_record status to see available indices.

name: time_control
description: Pause / resume / step the game via Time.timeScale.

name: events_query
description: Read the unified event log. Categories: log.log/log.warning/log.error/log.exception, ui.click/ui.down/ui.up/ui.change/ui.focus/ui.blur/ui.keydown/ui.wheel/ui.submit/ui.move, trace, watch, trigger, scene, custom. A category prefix (e.g. 'ui', 'log') matches all sub-categories.

sinceSeq.description: Only events after this seq. Omit to get the most recent ones.

name: events_config
description: Enable/disable event categories (ui.move is off by default), clear the log, view per-category counts, or capture every thrown exception (even caught ones). Example: firstChance=true firstChanceMax=500, then events_query categories=["exception.firstchance"] detail=true.

clear.description: Drop all stored events and error groups.

firstChance.description: Turn first-chance exception capture on or off (Mono only).

firstChanceMax.description: Stop capturing after this many exceptions (default 1000).

name: errors
description: Errors and exceptions logged since start, grouped by type and top stack frame with counts and first/last time; start here when something went wrong. Example: full=true limit=5 contains="NullReference".

full.description: Include the whole stack of the latest occurrence of each group.

contains.description: Filter by text in type, message or stack.

name: wait_for
description: Block until a condition is met or timeout. Any ONE of the given conditions ends the wait. Returns MATCHED/TIMEOUT plus a summary of everything that happened meanwhile. Pass sinceSeq from the preceding action so fast events are not missed.

contains.description: Substring the event text must contain.

ui_name.description: Wait for an element with this name.

ui_text.description: Wait for an element with this text.

gone.description: Invert the UI condition: wait until the element disappears.

equals.description: Expected formatted value of the state path. Omit to wait until the path resolves.

frames.description: Just wait this many frames (no other condition needed).

ms.description: Just wait this many milliseconds (no other condition needed).

name: scene_tree
description: GameObject hierarchy of all loaded scenes (incl. DontDestroyOnLoad) with component names.

root.description: GameObject path like /Root/Child to start from.

name: state_get
description: Read any value via reflection (private members included), page through big objects and collections, and get ids (#u.. Unity objects, #o.. other objects) that work as paths in every state tool. Example: path="/Game:Inventory.items" offset=30 limit=10 fields=["id","owner.name"] depth=2; path syntax '/Go/Path:Component.field.sub[0]', '@Namespace.Type.staticMember', '#u123:Rigidbody.velocity', '#o7.items[2]', '#12.text' (UI element).

depth.description: How deep to expand objects (default 1, max 4).

offset.description: Skip this many top-level entries (collection items or members).

fields.description: Only these members of the object (or of each item of a collection); paths like 'owner.name' work.

filter.description: Keep top-level entries whose name or value contains this text.

members.description: all (default, private included) | public | serialized (what Unity saves: public or [SerializeField], not [NonSerialized]).

props.description: Also evaluate public properties (default false; getters may have side effects).

name: state_query
description: Search, sort, group and summarize a large collection (100k items stay responsive: the scan is spread over frames); use it instead of paging state_get when looking for specific items. Example: path="/Game:Units.all" where=[{"field":"hp","op":"<","value":10}] select=["name","hp"] sort="-hp" limit=20, or group="team" stats=true.

path.description: State path of a list, array, set or dictionary (dictionary items have Key and Value).

where.description: Conditions, all must hold: {field, op, value}; op is == != < <= > >= contains; field '.' is the item itself. Numbers compare as numbers, text ignores case.

select.description: Fields to show per item (default: a one-line summary).

sort.description: Field to sort by; '-field' for descending.

stats.description: Count, item types, min/max/avg of numbers and unique count of text (for select fields, or for the items themselves).

name: state_export
description: Write a whole collection to a JSONL file (one item per line) for offline analysis when it is too big to read through the tools. Example: path="/Game:Orders.history" depth=2; the file goes to ~/.udriver/exports (owner-only, max 200 MB per file; the folder keeps 2 GB by default and deletes its oldest files first) and the reply gives its path, line count, size and the first 3 lines.

depth.description: How deep to serialize each item (default 2, max 4); Unity objects become {"$ref":"#u.."}.

name: state_set
description: Write a field/property via reflection.

path.description: State path ending in a member or index.

name: state_call
description: Invoke a method via reflection on the object at 'path' (or a static method if path is '@Type'); the overload is picked by the argument types. Example: path="@System.Math" method="Max" args=[1.5,2]; when several overloads fit equally, the error lists them and types=["double","double"] picks one.

path.description: State path of the target object, or '@Namespace.Type'.

types.description: Parameter type names that select the overload, e.g. ["string"].

name: types_find
description: Search loaded game types by name ('*' wildcards allowed). Use this to discover the code before placing probes.

name: type_members
description: List fields, properties and methods of a type.

name: watch_add
description: Probe: poll a state path every frame and emit a 'watch' event whenever its value changes.

name: trace_add
description: Probe: record calls of the matching methods as hits, optionally only when a condition holds, with captured values and stacks, or pause the game on a hit (needs 0Harmony.dll in the project; Mono only). Example: pattern="Game.Bank.Withdraw" when={"field":"amount","op":">","value":1000} capture=["this.balance","account.owner"] stack=true maxHits=5, then probe_list id=<probe>.

pattern.description: Namespace.Type.Method with '*' wildcards, e.g. Game.Orders.OrderService.* or *Algorithm*.Start

capture.description: Values to record per hit: paths starting with this, a parameter name or argN, e.g. this.hp, order.items[0].price.

when.description: One condition {field, op, value} (field as in capture; op == != < <= > >= contains); calls that fail it are only counted.

stack.description: Record the stack trace of each hit (default false).

pause.description: Pause on each hit: editor pause in the editor (resume with editor_play action=resume), timeScale=0 in a build (time_control action=resume).

maxHits.description: Record at most this many hits (default 2000; calls are still counted).

name: trigger_add
description: Probe: when a matching event occurs, run an action: pause (freeze time), capture_frame (store a frame in the frame buffer), mark (just emit a 'trigger' event). Optionally snapshot a state path at that moment.

state.description: State path to snapshot into the trigger event.

name: probe_list
description: List active probes (watches, traces, triggers) with hit counts, or read one trace probe's recorded hits page by page. Example: id=3 offset=0 limit=20.

name: probe_remove
description: Remove a probe. Probes set by other agents stay unless force=true.

force.description: Also remove probes set by other agents.

name: profiler_get
description: Current performance counters: frame time/fps, memory, GC, draw calls. 'add' registers extra counters ("Category/Name", see profiler_list).

name: profiler_list
description: List available profiler counters/markers in this build.

name: memory_summary
description: Memory at a glance, instantly: Unity used/reserved, managed heap, graphics, textures/meshes/materials/animations/RenderTextures/audio (count and bytes), object counts, GC allocations per frame. Start of a leak hunt: memory_summary -> memory_snapshot take -> play -> memory_snapshot diff -> memory_refs.

name: memory_top
description: Heaviest loaded Unity objects with id, bytes, size/format for textures, vertices/triangles for meshes; runtime=true marks objects made by code (not assets), unused=true runtime textures/meshes/materials no scene renderer or material uses. group=true totals by type. Example: type=Texture2D runtime=true limit=10.

type.description: UnityEngine.Object type name: Texture, Texture2D, RenderTexture, Mesh, AudioClip, Material, Shader, AnimationClip, GameObject... (default: all objects).

group.description: Totals per type instead of single objects.

name: memory_snapshot
description: Light snapshots of all Unity objects (count and bytes per type plus object ids), kept per agent (max 5), and diffs between them: what was added or grew, with the new objects listed by id. Example: action=take name=before, play, then action=diff from=before (compares with now).

name.description: Snapshot name for take/drop (default s1, s2...).

from.description: For diff: base snapshot (default your latest).

limit.description: Types and new objects to show (default 15).

name: memory_watch
description: Sample memory several times while the game runs and report the trend per object type: bytes/s, count/s and whether it rises monotonically; finds what grows over a long session. Example: samples=10 intervalMs=1000.

timeoutMs.description: Allow samples x intervalMs beyond 100 s (up to 600000).

name: memory_refs
description: Who keeps an object alive: shortest reference paths from static fields of game code, scene components and DontDestroyOnLoad to it, as state paths like @Game.Cache.items[3]. The same walk finds destroyed Unity objects still referenced from code and the biggest collections. Example: id="#u-4242" (from memory_top or memory_snapshot diff), or find=all.

id.description: Object id #u.. or #o.. to find holders of.

find.description: holders (default with id) | destroyed | collections | all (default without id).

from.description: Walk only from this state path instead of all roots.

offset.description: Skip this many entries of the destroyed/collections lists.

limit.description: Paths or entries to show (default 5 paths, 20 entries).

name: memory_capture
description: Write a full memory snapshot (.snap for the Unity Memory Profiler package) to ~/.udriver/exports (owner-only; the folder keeps 2 GB by default and deletes its oldest files first) and return its path and size; editor or Development Build only. Use it when memory_snapshot and memory_refs are not detailed enough.

name: render_stats
description: Measure rendering over N frames: frame time min/avg/p95/max and spikes, CPU main/render thread and GPU time, what bounds the frame, draw calls, batches, SetPass calls, triangles, vertices, shadow casters, RenderTexture count and memory. Start here when the frame is slow, then render_scene.

name: render_scene
description: What is drawn and why it costs: render pipeline, quality, vsync, screen; cameras (order, target, culling mask, clear flags, size); visible renderers sorted by triangles or materials with shaders; lights and shadows; hints on what breaks batching. Example: camera="Main Camera" sort=materials limit=10.

camera.description: Only this camera (name, GameObject path or #u id).

name: screen_pick
description: What is under a screen point: UI Toolkit element, uGUI raycast hits, and scene objects whose renderer bounds the camera ray crosses.

name: locate
description: Where a GameObject is on screen (to click 3D/2D world objects with x,y + method=input).

name: batch
description: Run several tools in one round trip, in order. Output of each call is concatenated.

calls.description: Items: {"tool":"ui_click","args":{...}}, optionally with "target" (next to tool or inside args) and "quiet":true (drop this call's output unless it fails) (max 50). Steps may mix games, editor_*, app_* and targets.

stopOnError.description: Stop at the first failing call (default true).

output.description: all (default) | last (only the last call's output) | errors (only failing calls). Failing calls are always shown.

name: self_test
description: Driver diagnostics: builds a temporary UI and verifies that every core capability really works in this project/build (tree, click, typing, keys, drag, scroll, value setting, screenshots, events, reflection, watches, input injection, uGUI, memory, rendering). Run once after installing; report the output if something fails.

name: editor_status
description: Editor state: Unity version, project, Play Mode, compiling, compile errors, open scenes, last test run and build.

name: editor_play
description: Control Play Mode. Entering/leaving Play Mode reloads scripts, so the driver is briefly unreachable; then use app_connect.

action.description: play | stop | pause | resume | step (true single-frame step).

name: editor_compile
description: Script compilation: current state and the list of compiler errors with file and line. action=refresh re-imports assets and recompiles.

name: editor_tests
description: Unity Test Framework. action=run starts EditMode or PlayMode tests (optionally filtered), status shows progress, results lists outcomes with messages and stack traces.

groups.description: Regex groups (e.g. namespace or fixture names).

onlyFailed.description: For results: only failed tests (default true).

name: editor_build
description: Build a player from the editor (Development Build by default so the driver is active). The editor is blocked while building; poll with action=status.

path.description: Absolute output path inside an approved build folder: Game.exe on Windows, Game.app on macOS, Game.x86_64 on Linux, e.g. C:/Builds/QA/Game.exe.

scenes.description: Scene paths (default: enabled scenes from Build Settings).

name: editor_scene
description: Scenes in the editor: list (open scenes + Build Settings), open a scene by asset path, or save open scenes.

name: editor_assets
description: Search project assets (AssetDatabase.FindAssets syntax, e.g. 't:VisualTreeAsset order', 't:Scene', 't:Script Trade').

folder.description: Limit to a folder, e.g. Assets/UI.

name: editor_menu
description: Execute an editor menu item by path, e.g. 'Assets/Refresh' or a project's custom menu.
